messages:
Erin: Quick sync — I've sketched a Customer Egress + Network Contract Playbook for private deployments. Goal: one-page runbook for SEs + Ops to close network handoffs. Need acceptance criteria, edge-case fallbacks, and SLA language. Ping @Raj for networking, @Leah for product, @Chris for SRE.

Raj: Ack, will look. Do we want to support both 'customer NAT' and 'customer BGP' options? Edge cases: asymmetric routing & return-path weirdness.

Leah: We need to capture negotiation triggers: env constraints (air-gapped), compliance reqs, and whether customer will provide public IPs. Also add rollback criteria and sign-off gates.

Chris: From ops side: must include health-check endpoints, port whitelist, MTU expectations, and monitoring hooks. If customer-managed egress fails, do we want auto-fallback to Redwood-hosted egress for critical paths?

Erin: Thinking fallback flow: prefer customer-managed when connectivity is healthy for 24h; if health checks fail 3 consecutive times (5m interval) then failover. Draft snippet:

```yaml
egress_fallback:
  checks: ["tcp:443", "http:/healthz"]
  consecutive_failures: 3
  check_interval_sec: 300
  rollback_action: "route-via-hosted-egress"
```

Raj: Need to call out BGP communities and MEDs. Also if customer blocks our source IPs during failover, we must ensure graceful retry window. Add explicit ACL and DNS expectations (no hairpinning, no full-proxy).

Leah: Acceptance criteria (first pass):
- customer provides documented IP ranges, ASN, and routing policy
- successful cross-verify of BGP session in staging
- perf: p95 latency increase < 20% vs hosted baseline
- documented rollback and runbook validated in staging

Chris: Add: observability hooks:
- prometheus:net_conn_up{customer=\"X\"}
- synthetic probe every 60s from 3 regions
- alert: egress-down after 5m + ops paging

Erin: Great. Two open questions:
1) Contract language for 'customer changes IPs without notice' — propose reschedule window 72h and emergency override clause.
2) How to model cost allocation for bandwidth egress when on customer side?

Raj: For 1) agree 72h. For 2) we should include optional metering tag to attribute usage; billing team needs to sign off. Mark 'billing: TBD' in PRD for now.

Leah: I'll draft a PRD section for negotiated SLAs + billing notes. Also propose acceptance sign-off checklist:
- [ ] Network diagram uploaded to customer portal
- [ ] BGP session established in staging
- [ ] Healthcheck probes green for 24h
- [ ] Failover validated manually
- [ ] Runbook rehearsed with SE + Ops

Erin: Can someone paste a short sample BGP export policy we can use? Raj?

Raj: Sample (minimal):

```
neighbor 203.0.113.2 remote-as 65100
neighbor 203.0.113.2 description "Customer Egress"
neighbor 203.0.113.2 ebgp-multihop 2
route-map EXPORT-CUSTOMER permit 10
  set community 65000:100
```

Chris: Notes on edge cases: asymmetric MTU -> path MTU discovery disabled in some customers; we should require PMTU >= 1400 or enforce fragmentation. Add to acceptance criteria.

Erin: Nice. I'll incorporate and update the central doc. Ops-bot: please post the current draft link.

ops-bot: Document created: https://docs.redwood.ai/private-deploy/playbooks/customer-egress-playbook-draft — tag: draft-v0.1 :robot_face: 

Leah: I'll add billing stub and tie to PRD. Let's try to get sign-offs from Legal on 72h change policy before next week.

Raj: I'll prepare BGP checklist and sample configs for AWS VGW, GCP CloudRouter, and bare-metal edge.

Chris: Plan ops runbook rehearsal Thu 11am PT — anyone conflict? (note: moved from 10am)

Erin: 11am works for me. Leah?

Leah: Free.

Raj: I had a customer call at 10 so 11 is better.

Leah: One last thing — test scenario where customer partially filters our CIDR range causing partial failures. Add to edge-case test matrix.

Erin: Good catch. Add test: 'partial CIDR filtering' with expected behavior = route sensitive traffic via hosted fallback, degrade non-critical features.
